newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rises to back to three percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money rises to back to three percent.

text.p: German call money rates rose back to the repo rate at three percent on Monday as market liquidity returned to normal following a glut of funds at the end of May which had pushed the call rate below three percent.

Commercial banks' effective deposits slipped to 42.9 billion marks on Friday from 44.6 billion on Thursday, while the average for the month through Saturday rose to 41.3 billion marks from 41.1 billion. Borrowing from the bank's Lombard facility totalled about 100 million marks on Friday compared with 300 million on Thursday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average rose to 3.05000 percent on Monday from 2.64000 percent on Friday.
